entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 43 Is 43:1-28 . A Succession of Arguments Wherein Israel May Be Assured that, Notwithstanding Their Perversity towards God ( Is 42:25 ), He Will Deliver and Restore Them. 1. But now-- notwithstanding God's past just judgments for Israel's sins. created-- not only in the general sense, but specially created as a peculiar people unto Himself ( Is 43:7 , 15, 21; Is 44:2 , 21, 24). So believers, "created in Christ Jesus" ( Ep 2:10 ), "a peculiar people" ( 1Pe 2:9 ). redeemed-- a second argument why they should trust Him besides creation. The Hebrew means to ransom by a price paid in lieu of the captives (compare Is 43:3 ). Babylon was to be the ransom in this case, that is, was to be destroyed, in order that they might be delivered; so Christ became a curse, doomed to death, that we might be redeemed. called ... by ... name-- not merely "called" in general, as in Is 42:6 ; 48:12 ; 51:2 , but designated as His own peculiar people (compare Is 45:3 , 4 ; Ex 32:1 ; 33:12 ; Joh 10:3 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9135"/><div sID="gen15488" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9135"/><hi type="bold">3. Egypt for thy ransom--</hi>Either Egypt or Israel must perish; God chose that Egypt, though so much more mighty, should be destroyed, in order that His people might be delivered; thus Egypt stood, instead of Israel, as a kind of "ransom." The Hebrew, kopher, means properly "that with which anything is overlaid," as the pitch with which the ark was overlaid; hence that which covers over sins, an atonement. Nebuchadnezzar had subdued Egypt, Ethiopia (Hebrew, Cush), and Saba (descended from Cush, <reference osisRef="Gen.10.7">Ge 10:7</reference>, probably Meroe of Ethiopia, a great island formed by the Astaboras and the Nile, conquered by Cambyses, successor of Cyrus). Cyrus received these from God with the rest of the Babylonian dominions, in consideration of his being about to deliver Israel. However, the reference may be to the three years' war in which Sargon overcame these countries, and so had his attention diverted from Israel (see on <reference osisRef="Isa.20.1">Is 20:1</reference>) [Vitringa]. But the reference is probably more general, namely, to all the instances in which Jehovah sacrificed mighty heathen nations, when the safety of Israel required it. <div eID="gen15488" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9136"/><div sID="gen15489" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9136"/><hi type="bold">4. Since--</hi>All along from the beginning; for there was never a time when Israel was not Jehovah's people. The apodosis should be at, "I will give." "Since ever thou wast precious in My sight, honorable, and that I loved thee, I will give," &c. [Maurer]. Gesenius, as English Version, takes "Since" to mean, "Inasmuch as." If the apodosis be as in English Version, "Since thou wast precious" will refer to the time when God called His people out of Egypt, manifesting then first the love which He had from everlasting towards them (<reference osisRef="Jer.31.3">Jr 31:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.11.1">Ho 11:1</reference>); "honorable" and "loved," refer to outward marks of honor and love from God.<div eID="gen15489" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15490" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">men ... people--</hi>other nations for thee (so <reference osisRef="Isa.43.3">Is 43:3</reference>).<div eID="gen15490" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15491" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thy life--</hi>thy person. <div eID="gen15491" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9150"/><div sID="gen15526" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9150"/>18. So wonderful shall be God's future interpositions in your behalf, that all past ones shall be forgotten in comparison. Plainly the future restoration of Israel is the event ultimately meant. Thus the "former things" are such events as the destruction of Sennacherib and the return from Babylon. "Things of old" are events still more ancient, the deliverance from Egypt and at the Red Sea, and entry into Canaan [Vitringa]. <div eID="gen15526" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9151"/><div sID="gen15527" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9151"/><hi type="bold">19. new--</hi>unprecedented in its wonderful character (<reference osisRef="Isa.42.9">Is 42:9</reference>).<div eID="gen15527" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15528" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">spring forth--</hi>as a germinating herb: a beautiful image of the silent but certain gradual growth of events in God's providence (<reference osisRef="Mark.4.26-Mark.4.28">Mr 4:26-28</reference>).<div eID="gen15528" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15529" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">way in ... wilderness--</hi>just as Israel in the wilderness, between the Red Sea and Canaan, was guided, and supplied with water by Jehovah; but the "new" deliverance shall be attended with manifestations of God's power and love, eclipsing the old (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.41.17-Isa.41.19">Is 41:17-19</reference>). "I will open a way, not merely in the Red Sea, but in the wilderness of the whole world; and not merely one river shall gush out of the rock, but many, which shall refresh, not the bodies as formerly, but the souls of the thirsty, so that the prophecy shall be fulfilled: 'With joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation'" [Jerome]. "A way" often stands for the true religion (<reference osisRef="Acts.9.2">Ac 9:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.18.26">18:26</reference>). "Rivers" express the influences of the Holy Spirit (<reference osisRef="John.7.37-John.7.39">Joh 7:37-39</reference>). Israel's literal restoration hereafter is included, as appears by comparing <reference osisRef="Isa.11.15">Is 11:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.11.16">16</reference>. <div eID="gen15529" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9158"/><div sID="gen15550" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9158"/><hi type="bold">26. Put me in remembrance--</hi>Remind Me of every plea which thou hast to urge before Me in thy defense. Image from a trial (<reference osisRef="Isa.1.18">Is 1:18</reference>; 41:1). Our strongest plea is to remind God of His own promises. So Jacob did at Mahanaim and Peniel (<reference osisRef="Gen.32.9">Ge 32:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.32.12">12</reference>). God, then, instead of "pleading against us with His great power," "will put His strength" in us (<reference osisRef="Job.23.6">Job 23:6</reference>); we thus become "the Lord's remembrancers" (<reference osisRef="Isa.62.6">Is 62:6</reference>, Margin). "Declare God's righteousness" vindicated in Jesus Christ "that thou mayest be justified" (<reference osisRef="Rom.3.26">Ro 3:26</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Isa.20.1-Isa.20.6">Is 20:1-6</reference>, and <reference osisRef="Ps.143.2">Psa 143:2</reference>). <div eID="gen15550" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 26. Put me in remembrance-- Remind Me of every plea which thou hast to urge before Me in thy defense. Image from a trial ( Is 1:18 ; 41:1). Our strongest plea is to remind God of His own promises. So Jacob did at Mahanaim and Peniel ( Ge 32:9 , 12 ). God, then, instead of "pleading against us with His great power," "will put His strength" in us ( Job 23:6 ); we thus become "the Lord's remembrancers" ( Is 62:6 , Margin). "Declare God's righteousness" vindicated in Jesus Christ "that thou mayest be justified" ( Ro 3:26 ; compare Is 20:1-6 , and Psa 143:2 ).

God, then, instead of "pleading against us with His great power," "will put His strength" in us ( Job 23:6 ); we thus become "the Lord's remembrancers" ( Is 62:6 , Margin). "Declare God's righteousness" vindicated in Jesus Christ "that thou mayest be justified" ( Ro 3:26 ; compare Is 20:1-6 , and Psa 143:2 ).
